import numpy as np
import json

# Calendar year surplus/deficit data from Treasury Bulletins (in millions)
# Extracting yearly totals (column 7 = Total surplus or deficit)
data = {
    1989: -152087,  # 1994 bulletin page 28
    1990: -220388,  # 1994 bulletin page 28
    1991: -268729,  # 1994 bulletin page 28
    1992: -290204,  # 1994 bulletin page 28
    1993: -254948,  # 1994 bulletin page 28
    1994: -203370,  # 1999 bulletin page 15
    1995: -163813,  # 1999 bulletin page 15
    1996: -107331,  # 1999 bulletin page 15
    1997: -22618,   # 1999 bulletin page 15
    1998: 70039,    # 1999 bulletin page 15
    1999: 125974,   # 2004 bulletin page 18
    2000: 236917,   # 2004 bulletin page 18
    2001: 127401,   # 2004 bulletin page 18
    2002: -157823,  # 2004 bulletin page 18
    2003: -374791,  # 2004 bulletin page 18
    2004: -412986,  # 2009 bulletin page 20
    2005: -318298,  # 2009 bulletin page 20
    2006: -248197,  # 2009 bulletin page 20
    2007: -161527,  # 2009 bulletin page 20
    2008: -454798,  # 2009 bulletin page 20
    2009: -1415722, # 2014 bulletin page 19
    2010: -1294204, # 2014 bulletin page 19
    2011: -1295591, # 2014 bulletin page 19
    2012: -1089353, # 2014 bulletin page 19
    2013: -680276,  # 2014 bulletin page 19
}

# Years 1989-2013 (25 years of data)
years = np.array(list(data.keys()))
values = np.array(list(data.values()))

print("Calendar year surplus/deficit data (1989-2013):")
for y, v in data.items():
    print(f"  {y}: {v:,}")

# Fit cubic polynomial: y = a*x^3 + b*x^2 + c*x + d
# Using year - 1989 as x to avoid numerical issues
x = years - 1989  # Now 1989 -> 0, 2013 -> 24

# Fit the polynomial
coeffs = np.polyfit(x, values, 3)
poly = np.poly1d(coeffs)

print(f"\nCubic polynomial coefficients:")
print(f"  a (x^3): {coeffs[0]:,.2f}")
print(f"  b (x^2): {coeffs[1]:,.2f}")
print(f"  c (x):   {coeffs[2]:,.2f}")
print(f"  d:       {coeffs[3]:,.2f}")

# Predict for 2025 (2025 - 1989 = 36)
x_2025 = 2025 - 1989
predicted_2025 = poly(x_2025)
print(f"\nCubic polynomial prediction for 2025: {predicted_2025:,.0f} million")

# Also fit using raw years for comparison
coeffs2 = np.polyfit(years, values, 3)
poly2 = np.poly1d(coeffs2)
predicted_2025_v2 = poly2(2025)
print(f"Using raw years prediction for 2025: {predicted_2025_v2:,.0f} million")
EOF
